AI compute infrastructure, Southeast Asia

We build and operate the infrastructure AI runs on.

The firm

Nourra Holdings is an AI compute infrastructure company headquartered in Singapore. We build and operate data centres designed for GPU clusters, with engineering and operations carried out by our own teams.

Value chain

Nine layers sit between a unit of electricity and a single model call.

Open each layer to see what it is and where Nourra sits.

Models and applications

Model training, inference services and enterprise AI applications. They decide how much compute is needed, where, and when.

Where Nourra sitsThe layer our clients and partners work in.

Compute services and cloud

Hardware turned into something you can rent: bare metal, GPU cloud, and model APIs billed by usage.

Where Nourra sitsWe arrange verified GPU capacity and enterprise cloud for partners.

Operations

Life after go-live: staffing, inspections, fault response, hardware replacement and expansion. Availability is defended at this layer.

Where Nourra sitsOur own on-site teams, delivered against a service level agreement.

Cluster deployment

Racking, cabling, power-up and commissioning once hardware arrives. A GPU cluster has thousands of cables, and one wrong run means rework.

Where Nourra sitsOur own engineering crews rack, cable and commission.

Networking and storage

The high-speed fabric that makes hundreds of servers behave as one machine, and the storage that holds training data.

Where Nourra sitsSpecialist engineers are assigned per project and named in the plan.

Chips and servers

GPUs, servers and full-rack systems. Supply is tight and lead times are long. This is the scarcest link in the chain.

Where Nourra sitsWe verify supply and lead times. Hardware goes straight into our own facilities.

Cooling

Carrying heat out of the rack. The newest full-rack GPU systems produce more heat than air can remove, so liquid runs directly across the chips.

Where Nourra sitsDesigned and built to high-density standards in our own facilities.

Building, mechanical and electrical

Structure, floor loading, transformers and switchgear, uninterruptible power and fire protection. A facility’s ceiling is set here.

Where Nourra sitsWe build our own data centres. Our crews handle electrical works and conversions.

Power and land

Substation capacity, power purchase and grid connection dates. How much power, and how soon, decides how large a facility can be and how fast it goes live.

Where Nourra sitsWe check power capacity, permits and power-on dates during site selection.

Inside the facility

An AI data centre does two things: it gets power into the rack and takes heat out.

Select a component to read about it.

  • Power
  • Coolant supply
  • Coolant return

Grid connection

The facility draws high-voltage power from the grid. How much capacity is available, and whether there are two independent feeds, is the first thing to confirm when choosing a site.

Transformers

They step high voltage down to what equipment can use. Total transformer capacity is, in practice, the ceiling of the facility.

Uninterruptible power

Batteries carry the load the instant the grid drops, until backup generators start. A GPU training run that loses power loses days of computation.

Power distribution

Power is split to every row and every rack. High-density racks need heavier busbars and a higher distribution rating.

Racks and GPU servers

Where the compute is. One current full-rack GPU system draws as much as a dozen or more conventional racks used to.

Coolant distribution unit

The heart of a liquid-cooled hall. It sends coolant to the cold plates in every server and brings the heated liquid back.

Heat rejection

Where the heat finally leaves the building. In a tropical climate like Singapore’s, this stage has a direct effect on the power bill.

Delivery

A cluster passes six gates between site selection and go-live.

Site and power

Confirm land use, floor loading, ceiling height and available power. Until power is secured, nothing after it stands.

Nourra’s partSite survey, and checks on power capacity, permits and power-on dates.

Design and approvals

Fix rack density, the power architecture and the cooling scheme, then complete drawings and approvals.

Nourra’s partWe organise design and coordinate approvals.

Building and M&E

Structural strengthening, transformers and switchgear, uninterruptible power, cooling pipework and fire protection.

Nourra’s partBuilt by our own engineering crews and accepted at milestones.

Arrival and racking

Servers, network equipment and full-rack systems arrive on site to be unpacked, racked, cabled and powered.

Nourra’s partWe verify supply and arrival dates. Our own crews rack and cable.

Commissioning

Network connectivity, full-load running and thermal validation. Problems found here cost far less than problems found after go-live.

Nourra’s partWe commission alongside specialist engineers and issue test records.

Handover and operations

The cluster is handed to its user and enters long-term operation.

Nourra’s partOur on-site team operates it against a service level agreement.

Principles

  • Our own teams

    The critical work is done by our own people. Responsibility stays in one place.

  • Compliance

    All business follows applicable export control and sanctions law. We confirm end user, location and use before we proceed.

  • Long-term partners

    We work with a limited number of partners over the long term, on written terms.
